name: Passkeys
description: Registers and signs in with passkeys through SwiftUI's authorization controller, returning the credential data your server verifies.

credentialsNeeded.description: Your domain (for example example.com) that serves apple-app-site-association and acts as the relying party
credentialsNeeded.whereToGet: A domain you control; host /.well-known/apple-app-site-association with a webcredentials entry for this app

cost.note: Apple Developer Program membership needed for device builds and distribution; simulator builds are free; needs your relying-party server and domain

amounts.label: Apple Developer Program membership (needed to distribute; not needed for simulator builds)

usage: In that view's file, `import AuthenticationServices` (Swift 6 requires the import where `AuthorizationController` is named) and read `@Environment(\.authorizationController) private var authorizationController` in the view that starts sign-in. Get a challenge (and for registration a user ID) from your server, then call `try await PasskeyService.fromBundle()?.register(userName:userID:challenge:using: authorizationController)` or `.signIn(challenge:using:)` and send the returned `PasskeyCredential` to your server to verify. Handle `PasskeyError.notConfigured` until ASSOCIATED_DOMAIN is set. Passkeys need a server; there is no local-only mode.
statusNote: Swift compiled on a Mac in the combined compile check (see compileCheck); the module's own verify run has not passed yet: `ios-agent-mcp capabilities verify passkeys` on a Mac.

compileCheck.scope: Template Swift and the verify usage file compiled with every other module in one app target (scripts/capability-compile-check.mjs, clean build in Xcode). Not covered: the XcodeGen project, entitlements, the widget extension target and runtime behavior.
